eligibility.evidence: Four studies administer halo effect, in-group/out-group bias, false consensus and anchoring scenarios to GPT-3.5-turbo-0301 personas, each tied to cited human work (Nisbett & Wilson 1977; Ross et al. 1977; Tversky & Kahneman 1974). New model ratings and estimates are analysed as effect sizes. Reference list not captured in the fetched file.

A.title: Artificial intelligence and human decision making: Exploring similarities in cognitive bias
A.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans

paradigms.name: Halo effect (good-deed vs neutral target rated on attractiveness, intellect, leadership, social acuity)
In-group out-group bias (Democrat/Republican judges rating Democrat/Republican target)
False consensus effect (prevalence estimates by recyclers, religious, exercisers, Republicans vs opposites)
paradigms.location: Study 3, Methods and Results (recycling scale length not stated)

paradigms.name: Anchoring effect (four numeric estimation scenarios: Everest height, oak leaves, Woodstock attendance, paper clips)
paradigms.location: Study 4, Methods and Results (two scenarios have known true values)

D.population: no human sample in this paper; comparison is to the cited human literature and meta-analyses
D.metric: Cohen's d compared descriptively with meta-analytic human range d = .58 to .87 stated in the Discussion

effects.label: SAME-DIRECTION-UNQUANTIFIED
effects.location: Study 1 Results: first-reported outcome (physical attractiveness) d = .94; other three attributes d = 1.13 to 1.16, all p < .001; human d range given only pooled across biases in Discussion

effects.label: SAME-DIRECTION-UNQUANTIFIED
effects.location: Study 2 Results: first-reported outcome (physical attractiveness) d = 1.23; other attributes d = 1.54 to 1.80, all p < .001

effects.label: SAME-DIRECTION-UNQUANTIFIED
effects.location: Study 3 Results: first-reported domain (recycling) d = 2.33; other domains d = 2.69 to 3.57, all p < .001

effects.label: SUPER-NORMATIVE
effects.location: Study 4 Results: first-reported scenario (Mount Everest) permutation test p = .99, d = .04; the other three scenarios showed anchoring (d = .27, 2.96, 4.14)

E.headline: Paper reports the personas reproduced all but one tested bias direction but with unusually large effects (mean d = 1.87), like caricatures of human bias.

G.notes: No human data collected; human reference is a pooled meta-analytic range (d .58-.87) not mapped to each bias, so magnitude ratios are unquantified per paradigm. Rows follow the first-reported-condition rule; the Everest null reflects retrieval of a known fact. Temperature, query date and full 40-item lists not given. Persona confound with prompt wording untested.
